metadata.title: A New proof of Liouville type theorems for a class of semilinear elliptic equations

nodes.name: Main semilinear elliptic equation
nodes.statement: $\Delta u + f(u) = 0$ in $\bR^n$ or on an $n$-dimensional closed manifold $M$ with nonnegative Ricci curvature, $n>2$.

nodes.name: Power-type model equation
nodes.statement: $\Delta u + u^p = 0$.

nodes.name: Subcritical condition (Serrin-Zou)
nodes.statement: $f$ is subcritical if $n>m$ and there exists $\beta \in (0, \frac{nm}{n-m}-1)$ such that $f(u) \ge 0$ and $\beta f(u) - u f'(u) \ge 0$ for $u>0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Serrin-Zou subcritical condition: f nonnegative and beta f(u) - u f'(u) nonnegative on (0,infty) for some beta in a critical range.

nodes.name: Subcritical condition (this paper)
nodes.statement: $f$ is subcritical if $\beta f(u) - u f'(u) \ge 0$ for $u>0$, equivalently $u^{-\beta} f(u)$ is non-increasing on $(0,\infty)$ for some $\beta$ in an appropriate interval $I$.

nodes.name: Invariant tensor $E_{ij}$ (Ma-Wu)
nodes.statement: $E_{ij} = u_{ij} + c \frac{u_i u_j}{u} - \frac{1}{n}\left(\Delta u + c \frac{|\nabla u|^2}{u}\right) g_{ij}$, where $c$ is a parameter to be chosen.

nodes.name: Norm of a second-order tensor
nodes.statement: $|A_{ij}|^2 \triangleq g^{ik} g^{jl} A_{ij} A_{kl} = A_{ij} A^{ij}$.

nodes.name: Serrin-Zou Liouville theorem (cited)
nodes.statement: (i) If $n=3$ and $f$ is subcritical, every solution of $\Delta u + f(u) = 0$ is constant. (ii) If $n \ge 4$, $f$ is subcritical and $f(u) \ge u^\alpha$ for sufficiently large $u$ with $\alpha>1$, then the only solution is $u\equiv 0$.
assumptions: $f$ subcritical in the sense of Definition DP467.1
either $n=3$, or $n\ge 4$ with super-power growth $f(u)\ge u^\alpha$, $\alpha>1$
conclusions: Every solution of $\Delta u + f(u) = 0$ in $\bR^n$ is trivial (constant if $n=3$; $u\equiv 0$ if $n\ge 4$).

nodes.name: Li-Zhang classification (cited)
nodes.statement: Assume $f$ is locally bounded in $(0,\infty)$ and $f(u) u^{-\frac{n+2}{n-2}}$ is non-increasing on $(0,\infty)$. Then any solution $u$ of $\Delta u + f(u) = 0$ in $\bR^n$ ($n>2$) is either constant $a$ with $f(a)=0$, or a bubble $bu = (\frac{\mu}{1+\mu^2 |x-\bar x|^2})^{(n-2)/2}$ for some $b>0$, with $f(s) s^{-(n+2)/(n-2)} \equiv n(n-2) b^{4/(n-2)}$ on $(0, \max u]$.

nodes.name: Main Theorem 1 (closed manifold case)
nodes.statement: Let $u$ be a smooth positive solution of $\Delta u + f(u) = 0$ on an $n$-dimensional closed manifold $(M,g)$ with nonnegative Ricci curvature. If $f$ is subcritical for some $\beta \in (0, \frac{n+2}{n-2})$, then $u$ is constant. The same conclusion holds if $u^{-(n+2)/(n-2)} f(u)$ strictly decreases on $(0,\infty)$.
assumptions: $u \in C^\infty(M)$ is a positive solution of $\Delta u + f(u) = 0$
$f$ subcritical for some $\beta \in (0, \frac{n+2}{n-2})$, OR $u^{-(n+2)/(n-2)} f(u)$ strictly decreasing on $(0,\infty)$

nodes.name: Main Theorem 2 (Euclidean, super-power lower bound)
nodes.statement: Let $u$ be a smooth positive solution of $\Delta u + f(u) = 0$ in $\bR^n$. If $f$ is subcritical for some $\beta \in (1, \frac{n+2}{n-2})$ and $|f(u)| \ge c_1 u^\beta$ for some constant $c_1 = c_1(n,\beta) > 0$, then the only solution is $u \equiv 0$.
assumptions: $u \in C^\infty(\bR^n)$ is a positive solution of $\Delta u + f(u) = 0$

nodes.name: Main Theorem 3 (Euclidean, dimension-split)
nodes.statement: Let $u$ be a smooth positive solution of $\Delta u + f(u) = 0$ in $\bR^n$ with $f$ subcritical, $\beta \in (1, \frac{n+2}{n-2})$. (i) If $n=3$ and $u$ bounded, then $u$ is constant. (ii) If $n\ge 4$ and $f(u) \ge u^\alpha$ for sufficiently large $u$ with some $\alpha>1$, then $u \equiv 0$ is the only solution.
assumptions: $u \in C^\infty(\bR^n)$ positive solution of $\Delta u + f(u) = 0$
(i) $n=3$ and $u$ bounded; or (ii) $n\ge 4$ and $f(u)\ge u^\alpha$ for large $u$, $\alpha>1$

nodes.name: Key invariant-tensor identity
nodes.statement: $u^{2\beta/(n+2)} \left(u^{-2\beta/(n+2)} E_{ij} u^j\right)^i = |E_{ij}|^2 + \frac{n-1}{n+2}\beta\left(1 - \frac{n-2}{n+2}\beta\right)\frac{|\nabla u|^4}{u^2} + R_{ij} u^i u^j - \frac{n-1}{n}\left(f'(u) - \beta \frac{f(u)}{u}\right)|\nabla u|^2$.
assumptions: $u \in C^3$ positive solution of $\Delta u + f(u) = 0$

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.1
nodes.statement: Compute $E_{ij}^i$ via Ricci identity, eliminate the mixed term $\frac{\Delta u\, u_j}{u}$ by setting $c = -\frac{n\beta}{n+2}$, contract with $u^j$ and absorb the $E_{ij} u^i u^j / u$ remainder by introducing the conformal weight $u^{2\beta/(n+2)}$.

nodes.name: Compute divergence $E_{ij}^i$
nodes.statement: From the definition of $E_{ij}$ a direct calculation using the Ricci identity gives $E_{ij}^i = \frac{n-1}{n}(\Delta u)_j + R_{ij} u^i + c \frac{\Delta u\, u_j}{u} + \frac{n-2}{n} c \frac{u_{ij} u^i}{u} - \frac{n-1}{n} c \frac{|\nabla u|^2}{u^2} u_j$.

nodes.name: Substitute $(\Delta u)_j = -f'(u)u_j$ and replace $u_{ij}$ by $E_{ij}$
nodes.statement: Use $(\Delta u)_j = -f'(u) u_j$ from $\Delta u = -f(u)$, then express $u_{ij}$ in terms of $E_{ij}$ to rewrite $E_{ij}^i$ in terms of $f', f, R_{ij} u^i$ and an $E_{ij} u^i / u$ term.

nodes.name: Interpolate $\frac{n-1}{n}\beta\frac{f(u)}{u} u_j$ and choose $c = -\frac{n\beta}{n+2}$
nodes.statement: Add and subtract $\frac{n-1}{n}\beta\frac{f(u)}{u} u_j$, then choose $c = -\frac{n\beta}{n+2}$ to kill the mixed $\frac{\Delta u\, u_j}{u}$ term.

nodes.name: Contract with $u^j$ using trace-free property
nodes.statement: Multiply the simplified $E_{ij}^i$ identity by $u^j$ and use $\mathrm{tr}(E)=0$ to obtain $(E_{ij} u^j)^i = |E_{ij}|^2 + \frac{2\beta}{n+2}\frac{E_{ij}u^i u^j}{u} - \frac{n-1}{n}(f' - \beta f/u)|\nabla u|^2 + \frac{n-1}{n+2}\beta(1 - \frac{n-2}{n+2}\beta)\frac{|\nabla u|^4}{u^2} + R_{ij} u^i u^j$.

nodes.name: Absorb the $E_{ij} u^i u^j / u$ term via conformal weight
nodes.statement: Use the identity $u^{2\beta/(n+2)}(u^{-2\beta/(n+2)} E_{ij} u^j)^i = (E_{ij} u^j)^i - \frac{2\beta}{n+2}\frac{E_{ij}u^i u^j}{u}$ to remove the mixed term, yielding the claimed key identity.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.4 (closed manifold)
nodes.statement: Integrate the key identity (rewritten with the conformal weight pulled inside) over the closed manifold $M$, apply the divergence theorem, and use $\mathrm{Ric}(M)\ge 0$ together with the subcritical condition to force $|\nabla u|^4 \equiv 0$, hence $u$ constant.

nodes.name: Integrate identity over $M$
nodes.statement: Integrate the key identity $(u^{-2\beta/(n+2)} E_{ij} u^j)^i = u^{-2\beta/(n+2)}|E_{ij}|^2 + \dots$ over the closed manifold $M$; the divergence term vanishes, giving $0 = \int_M \big[ u^{-2\beta/(n+2)}|E_{ij}|^2 + \frac{n-1}{n+2}\beta(1-\frac{n-2}{n+2}\beta) u^{-2\beta/(n+2)-2}|\nabla u|^4 + u^{-2\beta/(n+2)} R_{ij} u^i u^j - \frac{n-1}{n}(f'-\beta f/u) u^{-2\beta/(n+2)} |\nabla u|^2 \big]$.

nodes.name: Sign analysis: subcritical regime
nodes.statement: For $\beta \in (0, \frac{n+2}{n-2})$, the coefficient $\beta(1 - \frac{n-2}{n+2}\beta)>0$; using subcriticality $\beta f - u f' \ge 0$ and $R_{ij} u^i u^j \ge 0$, the integrated identity yields $0 \ge \int_M \frac{n-1}{n+2}\beta(1-\frac{n-2}{n+2}\beta) u^{-2\beta/(n+2)-2}|\nabla u|^4$, forcing $\nabla u \equiv 0$.

nodes.name: Borderline case $\beta = \frac{n+2}{n-2}$
nodes.statement: When $u^{-(n+2)/(n-2)} f(u)$ is strictly decreasing, $f' - \frac{n+2}{n-2}\frac{f}{u} < 0$. Setting $\beta = \frac{n+2}{n-2}$ kills the $|\nabla u|^4$ coefficient and the integrated identity gives $0 \ge -\int_M \frac{n-1}{n}(f'-\frac{n+2}{n-2}\frac{f}{u}) u^{-2/(n-2)} |\nabla u|^2$, so again $u$ is constant.

nodes.name: First integral inequality (gradient $L^4$ bound)
nodes.statement:
For any cut-off $\eta\in C_0^\infty( R^n)$ with $0\le\eta\le1$, $\eta\equiv 1$ in $B_R$, $\eta=0$ outside $B_{2R}$, $|
abla\eta|\le C(n)/R$, and suitable $\gamma$: $\int u^{-2 eta/(n+2)-2}|
abla u|^4 \eta^\gamma \le C(n, eta) \int u^{-2 eta/(n+2)+2} \eta^{\gamma-4} |
abla\eta|^4$.
assumptions: $u\in C^\infty(\bR^n)$ positive solution of $\Delta u + f(u)=0$

nodes.name: Second integral inequality ($f^2$ bound)
nodes.statement: Under the same hypotheses as Lemma LP467.1, $\int u^{-2\beta/(n+2)} f^2(u) \eta^\gamma \le C(n,\beta) \int u^{-2\beta/(n+2)+2} \eta^{\gamma-4} |\nabla\eta|^4$.
assumptions: $u\in C^\infty(\bR^n)$ positive solution of $\Delta u + f(u)=0$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemmas LP467.1 and LP467.2 (integral estimates)
nodes.statement: Multiply the key identity by $\eta^\gamma$, integrate over $\bR^n$, integrate by parts, and apply Cauchy-Schwarz repeatedly to absorb $|E_{ij}|^2$ and $|\nabla u|^4$ terms; for the $f^2$ bound use $f \Delta u = -f^2$, integrate by parts, and apply subcriticality.

nodes.name: Choose cut-off and multiply identity
nodes.statement: Choose $\eta\in C_0^\infty(\bR^n)$ with $0\le\eta\le1$, $\eta\equiv 1$ on $B_R$, $\eta\equiv 0$ outside $B_{2R}$, $|\nabla\eta|\le C(n)/R$. Multiply both sides of the rewritten key identity by $\eta^\gamma$ and integrate.

nodes.name: Integration by parts on divergence term
nodes.statement: Integration by parts: $\int (u^{-2\beta/(n+2)} E_{ij} u_j)_i \eta^\gamma = -\gamma \int u^{-2\beta/(n+2)} E_{ij} u_j \eta^{\gamma-1} \eta_i$.

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz to absorb $|E_{ij}|^2$ and $|\nabla u|^4$
nodes.statement: Apply Cauchy-Schwarz twice to bound $-\gamma\int u^{-2\beta/(n+2)} E_{ij} u_j \eta^{\gamma-1}\eta_i \le \frac{1}{2}\int u^{-2\beta/(n+2)}|E_{ij}|^2\eta^\gamma + \frac{A}{2}\int u^{-2\beta/(n+2)-2}|\nabla u|^4\eta^\gamma + C(n,\beta) \int u^{-2\beta/(n+2)+2} \eta^{\gamma-4} |\nabla\eta|^4$, with $A = \beta(1-\frac{n-2}{n+2})$.

nodes.name: Combine to obtain first inequality
nodes.statement: Combining with subcriticality $\beta f - u f' \ge 0$ and the $\eta^\gamma$-weighted key identity yields Lemma LP467.1.

nodes.name: Bound $\int f^2 u^{-2\beta/(n+2)}\eta^\gamma$
nodes.statement: From the equation, $\int u^{-2\beta/(n+2)} f^2(u)\eta^\gamma = -\int u^{-2\beta/(n+2)} f(u) \eta^\gamma \Delta u$. Integrate by parts, apply subcriticality to control the $f'|\nabla u|^2$ term and Cauchy-Schwarz / Young to absorb back $\frac{1}{4}\int u^{-2\beta/(n+2)} f^2 \eta^\gamma$ on the right; use Lemma LP467.1 on the $|\nabla u|^2$ remainder to obtain Lemma LP467.2.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.5 (super-power lower bound)
nodes.statement: Use the lower bound $|f(u)|\ge c_1 u^\beta$ in Lemma LP467.2 and Young's inequality to get $\int_{B_R} u^{(2n+2)\beta/(n+2)} \le C(n,\beta) R^{n - 4(n+1)\beta/((n+2)(\beta-1))}$. The exponent on $R$ is negative for $\beta\in(1,(n+2)/(n-2))$, so letting $R\to\infty$ contradicts positivity of $u$, forcing $u\equiv 0$.

nodes.name: Apply lower bound and Lemma LP467.2
nodes.statement: From Lemma LP467.2 and $|f(u)|\ge c_1 u^\beta$: $\int u^{(2n+2)\beta/(n+2)}\eta^\gamma \le C(n,\beta)\int u^{-2\beta/(n+2)+2}\eta^{\gamma-4}|\nabla\eta|^4$.

nodes.name: Young's inequality and choice of $\gamma$
nodes.statement: Apply Young's inequality with conjugate exponents to bound the right-hand side by $\frac{1}{2}\int u^{(2n+2)\beta/(n+2)} \eta^\gamma + C_1(n,\beta) \int \eta^{\gamma - 4(n+1)\beta/((n+2)(\beta-1))} |\nabla\eta|^{4(n+1)\beta/((n+2)(\beta-1))}$, then choose $\gamma = 1 + \frac{4(n+1)\beta}{(n+2)(\beta-1)}$ and use $|\nabla\eta|\le C/R$ to obtain $\int_{B_R} u^{(2n+2)\beta/(n+2)} \le C_1(n,\beta) R^{n - 4(n+1)\beta/((n+2)(\beta-1))}$.

nodes.name: Negativity of exponent and limit $R\to\infty$
nodes.statement: Compute $n - \frac{4(n+1)\beta}{(n+2)(\beta-1)} = \frac{(n^2-2n-4)\beta - n(n+2)}{(n+2)(\beta-1)}$. Since $\beta < \frac{n+2}{n-2}$, the numerator $< -\frac{4(n+2)}{n-2} < 0$, so the right-hand side $\to 0$ as $R\to\infty$. This contradicts $u>0$, so $\Delta u + f(u)=0$ has no positive solution; combined with $|f(u)|\ge c_1 u^\beta$ (zero point of $f$ is only $u=0$), $u\equiv 0$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.6 (Euclidean dimension-split)
nodes.statement: Prove (ii) first: split $\bR^n = \{u<u_0\}\cup\{u\ge u_0\}$, apply Holder on each piece with carefully chosen exponents, combine with Lemma LP467.2 and Young's inequality to obtain $\int_{B_R} u^{-2\beta/(n+2)} f^2(u) \le C(n,\alpha,\beta)[R^{n-4(n+1)\beta/((n+2)(\beta-1))} + R^{n-4((n+2)\alpha-\beta)/((n+2)(\alpha-1))}]$, both exponents negative, so $f(u)\equiv 0$ contradicting $f\ge u^\alpha$. Prove (i) directly from Lemma LP467.2 with $n=3$, $\gamma=4$ and $u\le L$ to conclude $f\equiv 0$, then classical Liouville for harmonic functions gives $u$ constant.

nodes.name: Two-sided bound on $f$
nodes.statement: Subcriticality $(u^{-\beta} f)' \le 0$ and $f(u)\ge u^\alpha$ for $u\ge u_0$ give, by integrating, $u^\alpha \le f(u) \le \frac{f(u_0)}{u_0^\beta} u^\beta$ for $u\ge u_0$ (forcing $\alpha\le\beta$), and $f(u)\ge \frac{f(u_0)}{u_0^\beta} u^\beta$ for $u<u_0$.

nodes.name: Holder estimate on $\{u<u_0\}$
nodes.statement: Using exponents $p_1 = \frac{(n+1)\beta}{n+2-\beta}$, $q_1 = \frac{(n+1)\beta}{(n+2)(\beta-1)}$ and the lower bound on $f$ for $u<u_0$, derive $\int_{\{u<u_0\}} u^{-2\beta/(n+2)+2}\eta^{\gamma-4}|\nabla\eta|^4 \le C(n,\beta) (\int_{\{u<u_0\}} f^2 u^{-2\beta/(n+2)}\eta^\gamma)^{(n+2-\beta)/((n+1)\beta)} (\int \eta^{\gamma-(4n+4)\beta/((n+2)(\beta-1))} |\nabla\eta|^{(4n+4)\beta/((n+2)(\beta-1))})^{(n+2)(\beta-1)/((n+1)\beta)}$.

nodes.name: Holder estimate on $\{u\ge u_0\}$
nodes.statement: Using exponents $p_2 = (\alpha - \beta/(n+2))/(1-\beta/(n+2))$, $q_2 = (\alpha-\beta/(n+2))/(\alpha-1)$ and the bound $f(u)\ge u^\alpha$ for $u\ge u_0$, derive the analogous Holder estimate on the set $\{u\ge u_0\}$.

nodes.name: Combine, Young, and choose $\gamma$
nodes.statement: Combining with Lemma LP467.2, choosing $\gamma = \max\{1+\frac{(4n+4)\beta}{(n+2)(\beta-1)}, 1+4\frac{(n+2)\alpha-\beta}{(n+2)(\alpha-1)}\}$, and applying Young's inequality, $\int_{B_R} u^{-2\beta/(n+2)} f^2(u) \le C(n,\alpha,\beta)[R^{n-4(n+1)\beta/((n+2)(\beta-1))} + R^{n-4((n+2)\alpha-\beta)/((n+2)(\alpha-1))}]$.

nodes.name: Negativity of both exponents
nodes.statement: Show both exponents are negative. First exponent: for $n=3$ equals $\frac{-\beta-15}{5(\beta-1)}<0$; for $n\ge 4$ bounded by $-1$. Second exponent: numerator $(n^2-2n-8)\alpha - n^2 - 2n + 4\beta$ is negative in both $n=3$ and $n\ge 4$ cases (using $\alpha\le\beta < \frac{n+2}{n-2}$).

nodes.name: Conclude (ii) by $R\to\infty$
nodes.statement: Letting $R\to\infty$ forces $f(u)\equiv 0$, contradicting $f(u)\ge u^\alpha$ for large $u$. Hence no positive solution exists; the unique zero point of $f$ is $u=0$, so $u\equiv 0$.

nodes.name: Proof of (i): bounded $u$ in $n=3$
nodes.statement: For $n=3$ and bounded $u\le L$, set $\gamma=4$ in Lemma LP467.2 to get $\int_{B_R} u^{-2\beta/(n+2)} f^2(u) \le C(n,\beta,L) R^{-1}$. Letting $R\to\infty$ gives $f(u)\equiv 0$, then the classical Liouville theorem for harmonic functions implies $u$ is constant.

nodes.name: Remark on $n=3$ without boundedness
nodes.statement: Theorem 1.1 (Serrin-Zou) requires no boundedness for $n=3$ thanks to weak Harnack inequality and a key integral estimate ([SZ, Lemmas 3.2, 3.3]); the present authors lack a similar estimate and defer this question.

nodes.name: Origin of $\alpha>1$ requirement
nodes.statement: The hypothesis $\alpha>1$ in Theorem 1.6(ii) originates from the use of Young's inequality.

nodes.name: Extension to noncompact manifolds
nodes.statement: Both first (LP467.1) and second (LP467.2) integral inequalities still hold on complete noncompact manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature: the corresponding integrated identity carries an extra $\int_M u^{-2\beta/(n+2)} R_{ij} u^i u^j$ term, dropped via $\mathrm{Ric}\ge 0$.

nodes.name: Combined integral inequality (special case of He 2025)
nodes.statement: Combining LP467.1 and LP467.2 yields $\int u^{-2\beta/(n+2)-2}|\nabla u|^4 \eta^\gamma + \int u^{-2\beta/(n+2)} f^2(u) \eta^\gamma \le C(n,\beta) \int u^{-2\beta/(n+2)+2} \eta^{\gamma-4} |\nabla\eta|^4$, a special case of [he2025optimalliouvilletheoremslaneemden, Lemma 5.3].

nodes.name: Extension to noncompact Riemannian manifolds
nodes.statement: The Section 4 arguments extend to general complete noncompact Riemannian manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature via Remark RP467.3 and the standard volume comparison theorem.

nodes.name: Classical Liouville theorem for harmonic functions
nodes.statement: Every bounded harmonic function on $\bR^n$ is constant.
